Consumers purchase products and services to
experience certain emotional states or achieve emotional
goals in a process called emotional arousal. Emotions
can create a feeling of pleasure or satisfaction, but they
can also give the consumer the perception that their
purchase will help them avoid a feeling of displeasure.
No matter what the purchase is, consumers must
somehow associate a positive emotional connection
between a product and themselves. Positive emotions
can include the fulfillment of a desire or the feelings
of safety and protection. Consumers also have both
unexpressed and expressed emotions. It is important
to understand the difference between these emotions

People have often reported seeing animals, inanimate
objects, and people who have previously died. They
may be ‘ghosts’ or ‘angels’ and some involve quite
complicated scenes or bizarre situations. These are
known as hallucinations. Some visual hallucinations are
silent, but in some, people speak, often directly to the
individual experiencing the hallucination and give them
specific commands. But why do hallucinations occur?
There are a number of psychological explanations
for their occurrence. Freudians see hallucinations
as projections of unconscious wishes or wants. For
example, what a person experiences as “real” in a
hallucination is actually something they felt but could not
express because it was felt subconsciously. Cognitive
psychologists point to problems in cognitive processing,
particularly metacognition, which is concerned with the
understanding of others’ behaviours. However, it is the
biological psychologists who focus most clearly on the
causes. They see hallucinations primarily as deficits
in brain states resulting from damage and chemical
imbalances. They have been able to identify the chemical
processes that lead to hallucinations. Nevertheless,
explaining why a particular individual has a very
particular hallucination remains something of a mystery.

about the size of California. Roughly 1,600 km lie
between its southernmost and northernmost points.
About 15% of its area lies north of the Arctic Circle,
where, for a few days each summer, the sun never
sets, and never rises for a similar period in winter. The
Swedish climate is not severe, thanks to the warming
influence of the Gulf Stream. Only 7% of Sweden’s area
is cultivated farmland; more than half of the country is
covered by timberlands, consisting mostly of coniferous
forests. Mountains, fells, and wetlands occupy nearly a
quarter of the country. Sweden has about 100,000 lakes,
which include Vanern, the third-largest body of fresh
water in Europe. The Swedes are proud of the natural
beauty of their country and this large variety in landscape
makes Sweden a prime travel destination for outdoor
enthusiasts. Norrland, the northern three-fifths of the
country, is rich in natural resources, including timber, ore
deposits, and rivers, whose waterfalls contribute to the
national energy supply. It is here that the local indigenous
people earn their traditional livelihood herding reindeer.

dramatic increase in the quantity and intensity of human
loneliness, a rise that initially made these websites’

Under the Roman Republic, brickmaking, particularly in
the region of Rome itself, became a major industry, and
finally, under the Empire, it became a state monopoly.
Brick construction was cheaper than stone due to the
economies of scale in mass production and the lower
level of skill needed to put it in place. The brick arch
was adopted to span openings in walls. Mortar had
traditionally been composed of sand, lime, and water, but
beginning in the 2nd century BCE, a new ingredient was
introduced. The Romans called it pulvis puteoli after the
town of Puteoli (modern Pozzuoli), near Naples, where it
was first found. The material, formed in Mount Vesuvius
and mined on its slopes, is now called pozzolana. When
mixed with lime, pozzolana forms a natural cement that
is much stronger and more weather-resistant than lime
mortar alone, and that will harden even underwater.
Pozzolanic mortars were so strong and cheap, and
could be placed by labourers of such low skill, that the
Romans began to substitute them for traditional mortars
inside walls. The concrete made from pozzolana made it
possible to create curved shapes and led to the creation
of a series of remarkable interior spaces spanned by
domes and columns.

world, and have even conquered extreme habitats
such as deserts and the Arctic. In spite of all external
diversities, they have numerous characteristics in
common. Mammals are the most highly developed
vertebrate animals. Their constant body temperature

Prediabetes is a precursor to type 2 diabetes, but that
diagnosis does not necessarily mean diabetes is your
destiny. “Once you have diabetes, you cannot become
un-diabetic—but you can reverse prediabetes,” says

University Feinberg School of Medicine. Prediabetes
means the body struggles to use or produce the
hormone insulin, making blood sugar (glucose) zoom
to abnormally high levels, but not quite high enough to
be considered full-blown diabetes. A third of American
adults are estimated to have it, and your risk is higher if

you are over 45, or you have had gestational diabetes.

progress to the full disease, taking steps to make some
lifestyle changes such as a healthy Mediterranean diet
and more exercise to control blood sugar can help
stave it off. That is crucial: Type 2 diabetes increases
risks for chronic health problems like heart disease,
stroke, and impaired nerve, eye, and kidney function.

The origins of sociology and the coining of the term
by Auguste Comte, one of the important thinkers in
the history of the discipline, are usually traced back to
1839. However, others trace intellectual concern for
sociological issues much further back, and it could be
argued that scholars have been thinking sociologically
since the early history of humankind. However, it was
not until about a half-century after Comte’s creation of
the concept that sociology began to develop as a formal
and clearly distinct discipline, primarily in Europe and
the United States. It was another French thinker, Émile
Durkheim, who in the late 1800s was responsible for
distinguishing clearly the subject matter of sociology from
neighbouring fields such as psychology and biology.
Sociology became institutionalised in France, as well as
in Germany, Great Britain, and the United States. While
sociology in the United States did not take the early lead
in the development of key ideas and theories, it did move
strongly in the direction of institutionalisation.

The standard definition of creativity focuses on product:
a creator is someone who produces something novel
within a domain. This definition refers to the kind of
domain-changing creativity, called Big-C creativity.
Big-C creativity describes revolutionary contributions like
Thomas Edison’s invention of the light bulb, while Little-C
creativity refers to ordinary actions such as creating a
new recipe. Which of these do children demonstrate?
Given that one must master a domain, said to take about
ten years, before one can change it, then by definition no
child can be a Big-C creator. Typical children are Little-C
creators. Even child prodigies cannot be considered
creative in the Big-C sense: Mozart’s 5-year-old
composition, Minuet and Trio in G major, was stunning for
a 5-year old, but it did not change the domain of classical
music. But, Mozart’s childhood creativity is qualitatively
distinct from the creative play seen in a typical preschool
classroom, and this has led to the concept of Mini-C
creativity. Unlike the Big/Little categories, which focus
on creative production, the Mini-C category emphasises
the creative process. Mini-C creativity refers to the novel
and personally meaningful interpretation of experiences,
actions, and events. It aligns with the Vygotskian
conception of creative development, which suggests that
all individuals possess creative potential that begins with
an internalisation of cultural tools, not just copying but
rather filtering incoming information through pre-existing
knowledge.

to recognise the world. Egan proposes that children
aged 4 to 10, who are in the ‘mythic’ layer, puzzle out
the world by resorting to emotional categories, such as
love, hate, fear, joy, and to morals (principles of good
behaviour). They want to know how to feel about what

all bad; the perfect princess is all good. In order to plan

In the earliest days of air transportation, plane crashes
yielded few clues for safety investigators. Investigators
would struggle to figure out what happened immediately
preceding the accident but often fail to come to any
definite conclusions regarding the cause of the crash.
In one of those early days of civil aviation, a plane
crashed while landing in Australia. Despite intensive
investigations, the underlying cause for the accident was
never determined. The mystery prompted the Australia
Board of Inquiry to recommend that all airplanes be fitted
with a flight data recorder (FDR) that would detail the
flight crew’s conversation. Actually, efforts to make the
FDR a mandatory part of civil aircraft date back to the
early 1940s. The idea, however, faced one enormous
technological challenge. Design specifications required
that the unit survive the forces of an aircraft crash, as
well as any resulting fire exposure. In 1953, Australian
aviation scientist David Warren invented a fully automatic
‘Flight Memory Unit.’ His prototype could record cockpit
noise and instrument readings and remain intact
following a crash or fire. Much to Warren’s surprise,
Australian aviation experts and pilots originally rejected
the idea, on the premise of privacy issues. Warren took
the concept to the United Kingdom, where it was well
received by aviation officials. By 1957, the device was in
production.

is worried about her mother’s health. You try to
empathise with her situation and console her by
saying: ----

secenekler.A:
Your mother’s surgery is a major one and the
chances of a full recovery seem a bit low. Good
luck to your mom.
secenekler.B:
The doctors and nurses in this hospital are very
well-trained. If I needed surgery, I guess I would
also choose this hospital.
secenekler.C:
Why don’t you take your mother to another
doctor for a second opinion? This might help you
feel much better and get rid of your doubts.
secenekler.D:
I know it’s difficult when our loved ones are ill,
but I’m sure the operation will go well and your
mother will feel better in a very short time.
secenekler.E:
Actually, my friend Jane’s mom had the same
operation three times. But she still has a lot of
pain, so I hope your mother’s will go better.

soru:
You suddenly realise that you’ve completely
forgotten that yesterday was your best friend’s
birthday, because you’ve been so busy
studying. You sincerely apologise to your
friend and say you’ll make up to her for it: ----

secenekler.A:
I’m so sorry I forgot about your birthday. I
thought it was in summer.
secenekler.B:
My heartfelt apologies for forgetting your
birthday. Let me take you to dinner to celebrate.
secenekler.C:
Sorry I forgot, but I don’t understand why some
people are so obsessed with birthdays.
secenekler.D:
Forgive me for not buying you a present you’d
like. Let’s celebrate next year.
secenekler.E:
I didn’t mean to forget your birthday, but I’ve just
been so busy this week.

soru:
You couldn’t hand in your assignment on time,
so you lied to your teacher about your mother
being sick in hospital. The next day, your
teacher found out the truth, then she phoned
your mother. You are ashamed of what you did,
and you apologise to your teacher: ----

secenekler.A:
It’s a shame my mother didn’t back me up. I
won’t ever talk to her again.
secenekler.B:
I regret lying to you, but that’s my habit, and I
can’t help it. But why did you call my mother?
secenekler.C:
Sorry, I shouldn’t have lied. The truth is I played
computer games instead of doing the homework.
secenekler.D:
Sorry, I should have told you the truth. But then,
you would have been worried about my mother.
secenekler.E:
I apologise to you for not handing in the
assignment, but you had given us so little time to
finish it.

soru:
Your friends have invited you to a concert;
however, you have already made plans with your
grandmother to go shopping for an upcoming
special occasion. So, you tactfully decline their
offer by saying: ----

secenekler.A:
Sure, as soon as I finish shopping with my
grandmother, I’ll be at the concert hall. See you
all there!
secenekler.B:
Thanks for the invitation guys, but I’ve promised
my grandma that I’d help out with some
shopping as we have a party coming up.
secenekler.C:
I’d rather spend the day with my grandmother
shopping than go see a concert with you. It just
doesn’t sound fun to me.
secenekler.D:
I’m afraid I’ll have to pass. I’ve promised my
grandma that we’d hang out together and then
see a concert.
secenekler.E:
I can’t believe my favourite singer is in town.
Can I also bring my grandma to the concert?

soru:
Your friend is going to run in a marathon but is
doubtful if she can complete the race because
she has recently been ill. Now that she is feeling
better, you want to encourage her before she
runs the race, so you say: ----

secenekler.A:
Good luck, running in a marathon is difficult and
now it will be even more challenging.
secenekler.B:
Is this a good idea? Some runners can become
ill when running such a long distance.
secenekler.C:
You’ve worked hard to be in this marathon, and
I’m sure you’ll do great from start to finish.
secenekler.D:
Why don’t you consider running in next year’s
marathon, instead? I’m sure you can do it then.
secenekler.E:
You don’t have the courage to run a marathon
because you’re disadvantaged from the start.

soru:
One of your friends has asked you to check his
project work before submitting it, but because of
your own commitments, you lack the time to do
it. You want to let him know about the situation
without offending him, so you say: ----

secenekler.A:
I wish you had given it to me days before. How
can you expect me to do it in such a short time?
You know I’m busy.
secenekler.B:
Why don’t you ask another friend for help? I
wish I could help you, but I’m clueless about the
content of the project.
secenekler.C:
I really would like to help you but I’m really very
busy. I wish I had enough time. I’m very sorry.
secenekler.D:
I’m sorry, I suppose you’d better do it yourself,
it’s your own responsibility. I can’t spare any
time.
secenekler.E:
Do you think it’d be better if you asked your
teacher to change the deadline? Otherwise, it
won’t be possible to finish it.

soru:
suddenly you bump into a woman carrying
several grocery bags and cause her to drop her
groceries all over the ground. You feel terrible
for the accident and say to her: ----

secenekler.A: Hey lady! Watch where you’re going!
secenekler.B: Excuse me? Why would I help with those?
secenekler.C:
Sorry, but that shop should offer higher quality
grocery bags so accidents like this won’t
happen.
secenekler.D:
I guess if we were both paying attention this
would have never happened.
secenekler.E:
I’m so sorry! Here, let me help you with your
things.

soru:
You go to a restaurant for lunch and pay with
your credit card. When you check your bank
statement later on, you realise the cashier has
charged you more than your actual bill. So you
call the restaurant and ask politely: ----

secenekler.A:
Your waiter charged me more than the amount
of my bill. Put yourself in my shoes, can you
imagine my frustration?
secenekler.B:
I’ve just realised that I paid more than the bill by
mistake. Have you ever thought about firing your
overcharging cashier?
secenekler.C:
I think there’s been a mistake with my bill. Would
it be possible to correct it and give me a refund?
secenekler.D:
I’m busy with too many things at the moment
and now look what you’ve made me deal with.
waiters?
secenekler.E:
I don’t remember his name, but the waiter gave
me the wrong bill. Can you check what’s going
on?

soru:
Your teenage son asks for your permission to
go on a five-day camping holiday with one of
his friends, Jason. You think Jason has a bad
influence on your son and a long holiday might
make things even worse, so you firmly refuse to
give permission: ----

secenekler.A:
Sorry dear, but such a long trip would definitely
be a disaster with Jason. So, we need to discuss
it.
secenekler.B:
You know I don’t like Jason, but he may be good
fun on a trip.
secenekler.C:
Do whatever you want, just try to be firm with
Jason.
secenekler.D:
There’s no way I’ll allow you to take that trip with
Jason.
secenekler.E:
If you obey my strict rules, I won’t stand in your
way.

soru:
It is 1 a.m. and you have an important exam
tomorrow but your upstairs neighbour is having
a party with lots of people. Although you warned
them an hour ago, they are still very loud. You
go upstairs again and say angrily: ----

secenekler.A:
I’m really upset that you didn’t invite me to your
party.
secenekler.B:
If this party doesn’t end in ten minutes, I’m
calling the cops.
secenekler.C:
I wouldn’t do this to you if you had something
important to do the next day.
secenekler.D:
I really miss my old neighbours. They knew how
to throw a party.
secenekler.E:
This party is lame. All these people, but no one
to talk to.

soru:
You unexpectedly have a free weekend and
you heard that a friend has an exhibition of her
paintings at a café. You are eager to go and
you invite your best friend to join you. He says
he does not like such activities. So you say to
express your disappointment: ----

secenekler.A:
Even if you didn’t like the idea of an exhibition,
you could at least join me just to make me
happy. I felt excited about it.
secenekler.B:
I enjoyed it a lot when I last went there. She is a
great artist. I think we should give it a try.
secenekler.C:
I’m so indecisive about it. What do you think we
should do then if we don’t go to the exhibition?
secenekler.D:
I obviously chose a wrong activity for us. It’ll be a
total waste of time. What can we do instead?
secenekler.E:
I’ve been meaning to go to this exhibition for
weeks and you know it. Why do you always ruin
my plans?

soru:
You have a job interview but it is on the other
side of the town. You’re running a bit late. One
of your friends has a car and offers you a ride to
the interview. You accept the offer and gratefully
say: ----

secenekler.A: You really don’t have to. I can just take the bus.
secenekler.B:
I really appreciate your offer, but thanks. I can
probably make it if I run.
secenekler.C:
Thanks, this helps me a lot! I would miss the
interview if I took the bus.
secenekler.D:
Please do! I helped you wash your car, so you
actually owe me now.
secenekler.E:
Maybe I’ll just take the subway, it’s faster and
cheaper.

soru:
A friend of yours borrowed some money from
you a really long time ago and still has not paid
you back. You are really close friends and you
think he has simply forgotten. You don’t want to
upset him but want to make him understand that
you now need the money, so you say: ----

secenekler.A:
You always do this. You’re constantly asking for
money but you never pay it back. I always have
to remind you of it.
secenekler.B:
Please pay back the money you borrowed as
soon as possible. Otherwise, I’ll hire a lawyer
and take you to court!
secenekler.C:
Remember I lent you some money a while ago?
Don’t you think it’s time you paid it back? It’s
been ages!
secenekler.D:
I hate to bring this up, but I don’t think I’ll be
able to afford my expenses this month. So,
is it possible for you to return the money you
borrowed soon?
secenekler.E:
Do you remember when I lent you that money?
It’s been so long, and I don’t think I need it back
anymore. So, don’t worry about it.

soru:
Your new neighbours keep parking their car
in the place assigned to your flat rather than
using their own space, because yours is more
convenient for them. You have nicely reminded
them that it is not their parking space and
you have even had the apartment manager
remind them, but they just do not seem to care.
Completely furious by this point, you go to the
apartment manager and say: ----

secenekler.A:
My new neighbours have been using my parking
space. Can you please remind them not to use it
anymore?
secenekler.B:
You’ve got to do something else! This situation
is driving me crazy! Obviously reminding them
isn’t enough!
secenekler.C:
I’ve tried to warn them myself, but they don’t
seem to listen to me. Maybe you could ask them
to move their car.
secenekler.D:
You are so rude and disrespectful! Why do you
continue ignoring me?
secenekler.E:
I think the new neighbours and I have a small
problem. Maybe you would be able to help us
sort it all out.

soru:
It is your little daughter’s first day at school.
However, she is very nervous about making new
friends. You want to show that you understand
her and also you want her to socialise and have
fun. So you say to encourage her: ----

secenekler.A:
I know it is sometimes difficult to make new friends
at school, but can’t you at least try it for me?
secenekler.B:
While I was a student, I always had lots of
friends and we would enjoy ourselves a lot! I still
see some of them.
secenekler.C:
Why don’t you just relax? If you don’t like them,
you don’t have to talk to them!
secenekler.D:
I know how you feel, but when you have friends
around you, you can do many enjoyable
activities!
secenekler.E:
Never mind! You are such a lovely girl, you don’t
need many friends.

soru:
You had to hand in an assignment on Monday,
but you were ill over the weekend and so you
ask for a one-day extension. Your teacher asks
why you are requesting extra time. You want to
respond politely, so you say: ----

secenekler.A:
Here’s the doctor’s note. If you read it, you’ll
know why.
secenekler.B:
I’m really very sorry. I was quite ill over the
weekend.
secenekler.C:
Yes, I should have handed in the assignment
yesterday.
secenekler.D:
I was really ill. Can’t you tell by the way I look
today?
secenekler.E:
I think you’re one of the best teachers at our
school.

soru:
You have just started working at a small
successful company. One day, your brother
calls and asks you to buy him a new mobile.
However, with utilities, rent, and other expenses,
you are on a strict budget. So you have to
decline for now: ----

secenekler.A:
I’m sorry but money is a bit tight at the moment.
I promise I’ll get you one as soon as things start
to look up.
secenekler.B:
It all depends on the model you want. I won’t
get you an expensive one if you’re just going to
change it in a couple of months.
secenekler.C:
Since we live together and share the expenses,
you should be aware that we can’t afford a new
mobile now.
secenekler.D:
If you cannot bear the expense of a new mobile
yourself, I suggest you work harder and get a
high-paying job like mine.
secenekler.E:
I don’t have much money right now, but I’ll call
our parents and ask them to buy you a new
mobile.

soru:
Your friend has recently started painting.
Although she is not really good at it, she is overly
confident about her work. She shows you one of
her paintings and asks your opinion so you say
making fun of her: ----

secenekler.A:
It would be considered a masterpiece if you were
a three-year-old kindergarten student.
secenekler.B:
I’m really happy for you. You’ve found a hobby
that you’re happy with.
secenekler.C:
This is garbage. You’ve been taking lessons for
a month and this is all you can do?
secenekler.D:
I think you need to take more lessons to be a
good painter.
secenekler.E:
Even if you’ve just started, you did good enough.
It’s not too bad.

soru:
Your friend is planning a hike in an area which
is well-known for wild animals, such as bears,
wolves, and snakes. Because of the dangers
they pose, you want to warn your friend to be
careful, so you say: ----

secenekler.A:
That area is known to have wild animals. Hope
you can see some of them!
secenekler.B:
You know there are wild animals in that area.
Don’t call me if you get into trouble.
secenekler.C:
Take your camera so you can be sure to capture
any wild animals you see on film.
secenekler.D:
Stay alert while you’re there, and especially look
out for wild animals in the area.
secenekler.E:
Don’t worry if you see any wild animals. I’m sure
if you ignore them, they’ll ignore you.

soru:
Your friend is shopping for a dress for the
school prom and has just tried on a dress which
is really ugly. She likes the dress so much, but
when she asks you your opinion of the dress,
you want to tell her the truth. So trying not to
offend her, you say: ----

secenekler.A:
I don’t think that’s a good choice of dress for the
school prom. Why don’t you try some others?
secenekler.B:
To be honest, the dress looks great on you. But
isn’t it a bit revealing?
secenekler.C:
I can’t say anything really. You know I have a
poor taste in fashion.
secenekler.D:
It’s too expensive for such a plain and
unattractive dress. Don’t you think so?
secenekler.E:
Your parents would never allow you to put on
that dress for the prom. Let’s keep looking for a
better one, shall we?

soru:
While cleaning up your room in the attic, you
find an old book which belonged to a friend. You
realise that you were supposed to give it back to
her months ago. So you call her to apologise: ----

secenekler.A:
I apologise deeply for my mistake. However,
you should have reminded me to give back your
book.
secenekler.B:
I’m sorry to disturb you, but could you possibly
return the book that I lent you a few months
ago?
secenekler.C:
I would say I’m sorry, but since we are really
close friends and know each other well, I know
you’ll let this one go.
secenekler.D:
I regret to inform you that I have lost your
book. However, I will buy you an exact copy to
compensate for my mistake.
secenekler.E:
I’m so sorry for not returning your book on time,
I forgot all about it. I’ll get it back to you as soon
as I see you.

soru:
One of your workers is always late for work.
You’ve already warned him several times, but
he still keeps coming in late. Finally, you decide
you need to fire him. You ask him to come to
your office and say: ----

secenekler.A:
Despite repeated warnings, you continue to be
late. So, I’m sorry to inform you that you have
been terminated from your position.
secenekler.B:
We are actually content with your punctuality,
but I’m sorry to say to that you have been made
redundant at work.
secenekler.C:
This is the last time you will be warned about
coming to work late. The next time, you will
directly be sacked.
secenekler.D:
If I were you, I wouldn’t be late for work in the
future. The other employees think you are
getting preferred treatment from me and it’s
making my job more difficult.
secenekler.E:
If anyone asks, you can put the blame on me for
your coming late. They can’t fire me as I am your
boss.

soru:
You ordered a laptop from an online computer
company. When you receive your new laptop,
you notice that its battery does not seem to
function properly. So you call their customer
service line and politely ask for a refund: ----

secenekler.A:
The laptop I just got seems to have some kind of
problem. Could I possibly get my money back?
secenekler.B:
My laptop is not working properly. I think you
should send me a replacement as soon as
possible.
secenekler.C:
I would like to speak to your manager, urgently.
It’s about the laptop I recently bought.
secenekler.D:
If I don’t get my money back immediately, you
will be hearing from my lawyer!
secenekler.E:
It’s unfortunate that the laptop I bought has
problems. Still, I know you did your best.

soru:
A friend of yours is going to her high school
reunion party. She has just tried on some fancy
shoes and asks your opinion about them. You
don’t like them because you think the heels are
far too high. You suggest politely: ----

secenekler.A:
You can’t even walk with these shoes on! If you
buy them, you’ll fall down and look foolish at the
party.
secenekler.B:
It’s not worth buying new shoes for this
occasion. You already have several nice pairs at
home.
secenekler.C:
I think these might be a little bit too high for you.
Why don’t you try that pair over there?
secenekler.D:
Why are you even going to this party if you don’t
have a suitable pair of shoes to wear?
secenekler.E:
Let’s come back and try on these shoes later
after you’ve learned how to walk in heels.

soru:
Your friend celebrated his birthday but you
have been busy and failed to wish him a happy
birthday. Afraid you’ve hurt his feelings, you
want to extend an appropriate apology to him,
so you say: ----

secenekler.A:
I’ve been terribly busy recently. I’m so sorry I
forgot your birthday. Could you forgive me?
secenekler.B:
I’m so sorry I couldn’t be there to eat your
birthday cake. What kind was it?
secenekler.C:
If I kept a calendar, I could remember important
events like your birthday, don’t you think?
secenekler.D:
I’m sorry that I have a life of my own. You’re
always so sensitive about such things, aren’t
you?
secenekler.E:
Well, it’s okay that I forgot your birthday this time
around. There’s always next year, right?

soru:
One of your group mates is being lazy in
preparing the group project, which is due in
five days. You tried to drop some hints on
collaborative work but he just ignored those
remarks. The other group members asked you to
warn him one last time, so you say in a serious
manner: ----

secenekler.A: Unless you’re willing to work, we’ll get really upset.
secenekler.B:
We have someone else to help us out. So, you
don’t need to bother.
secenekler.C:
Don’t worry. We won’t tell the teacher you’re not
working.
secenekler.D:
We don’t get why you’re so lazy. Can’t you try
harder?
secenekler.E:
If you don’t help us with the project, you’ll be out
and fail the project.

soru:
Your daughter is a bright high-school student and
also into vlog videos on the Internet. One day,
she comes up to you and says that she wants to
leave the school and become a full-time vlogger.
and also you are aware of the importance of
education. So you say: ----

secenekler.A:
You know what? There are many successful
figures in history with very little education
background. I support you on your decision.
secenekler.B:
It’s perfectly fine to do the thing you love the
most, but your education cannot be put off.
I think it’d be better if you build up a balance
between school and vlogs.
secenekler.C:
I know assignments and presentations at school
can be challenging but being a vlogger is also
not as easy as it sounds.
secenekler.D:
I’ve read an article about how much money
vloggers make and got shocked! I think it’s best
to work towards that ambition of yours.
secenekler.E:
It’s your life, your decisions. We can arrange an
online education for you to improve your vlogs.
You should be the best at whatever you do.

soru:
You have recently arrived at your host university
with a study-abroad program. You have made
a friend from Spain but you are not sure how to
pronounce her name. So you politely ask her:
----

secenekler.A:
I’m sorry. Could you please tell me the exact
pronunciation of your name?
secenekler.B:
Your name is so long and difficult to say, do you
often have problems with how people pronounce
it?
secenekler.C:
Are all Spanish names as melodic sounding as
yours?
secenekler.D:
Would you like me to teach you how to correctly
pronounce my name?
secenekler.E:
Do you often get upset when people
mispronounce your name?

soru:
One of your colleagues has been given an
assignment that he’s not comfortable with. He
asks you whether you can help him. But you
also sense that he tries to make you do most of
the work for him. To comfort him and also avoid
doing the work, you say: ----

secenekler.A:
Why don’t you ask for help from someone else? I
get highly anxious when my workload increases.
secenekler.B:
You know you can handle this. As long as you
follow the guidelines that I gave you, you’ll be
successful.
secenekler.C:
You guys can’t get anything done around here. I
wonder how you could survive a day without me.
secenekler.D:
I’ll help you one last time, but you have to trust in
yourself and take action, or you’ll always depend
on others.
secenekler.E:
If you come up to me with this sort of thing
again, I’ll tell the manager that you’re not fit for
this job.

soru:
You’re invited to your new neighbour’s party.
When you arrive at his house, you’re surprised
to see that everyone’s wearing a costume.
Feeling awkward in a suit, you calmly say to the
host that he should have informed you to dress
in a costume: ----

secenekler.A:
I wish you had told me this was going to be a
costume party. I would’ve put on something
suitable.
secenekler.B:
You should know that you’re terrible at
organising a costume party. Look I came in a
suit!
secenekler.C:
Can you explain why you didn’t invite me to such
a fantastic costume party before?
secenekler.D:
You should’ve warned me that this would be
a hero costume party. I would’ve chosen a
different costume!
secenekler.E:
Everybody loves costume parties but me. I
shouldn’t have come here in the first place!

soru:
One of your friends has been following a strict
diet mainly consisting of fruits and vegetables,
and she does not consume any carbohydrates
or dairy products. Recognising the importance
of having a balanced diet to maintain good
health, you firmly warn your friend about this
issue: ----

secenekler.A:
I used to follow a strict diet years ago, but it
never worked for me. Even if your diet requires
drastic changes in your eating habits, you should
try to keep it.
secenekler.B:
Do you think it’s urgent for you to lose weight
rather than postponing it to summer time?
You’re already in good shape, but you risk losing
your health by starving yourself.
secenekler.C:
You can’t safely lose weight and get all of the
nutrients you need by only eating certain kinds
of food. You should definitely increase the
variety of foods in your diet to stay healthy.
secenekler.D:
It seems you’ve been overwhelmed by modern
trends, but you should confirm if they’re
adequately supported by dieticians. Otherwise,
you can’t lose weight as you’ve planned.
secenekler.E:
Having a strict diet may reduce your energy
level and make you feel physically and mentally
weak. If you have such symptoms, please don’t
hesitate to seek medical help.

soru:
One of your friends has invited you to do
yoga, but none of you has any knowledge
about how to practise yoga. Although she’s
very enthusiastic about it, you’re scared of
wasting your time with ineffective exercises or
even hurting yourself. So, you come up with a
solution not to frustrate her and say: ----

secenekler.A:
I’m longing to practise yoga with you, but I don’t
have the necessary equipment and outfit for it.
Shall we do shopping?
secenekler.B:
Why don’t we go outside to enjoy nature while
trying different yoga techniques?
secenekler.C:
I think it’d be the best for us to enrol in a yoga
class where we can get detailed guidance.
secenekler.D:
I’ve recently watched a movie about a young
yoga trainee, but I’m not sure we can practise
the same yoga positions.
secenekler.E:
As I injured my back in an accident last year, I
have to attend physiotherapy sessions, sorry.

soru:
You overhear some of your classmates
discussing that reading a print book is no longer
necessary since people can listen to audio
books or watch films based on such books. Yet,
you adopt a positive stance towards reading
print books and join the discussion: ----

secenekler.A:
Well, that might be the case for some people.
However, there’s no doubt that reading printed
books enhances our imagination and creativity.
secenekler.B:
I agree that audio books are more convenient
for many. But we should be careful about
which audio books we choose. They should be
narrated by professionals to convey an accurate
message.
secenekler.C:
You know, I think if we’re to support writers, we
should first buy print books and then listen to
audio books or watch films. This makes me feel
less guilty.
secenekler.D:
I know writers spend enormous time and effort
producing their works, but it could be far more
challenging for film directors to convert a written
work into a movie with attractive scenes.
secenekler.E:
Though I like reading, I’d rather watch films.
I believe they can picture the characters and
events in a more vivid way than audio books.
Also, we can save trees by avoiding printing.

soru:
One of your colleagues plans to quit his stable
job to start a risky business venture without
gathering adequate information and preparing
properly. Realising how important it is to think
carefully before making a big move, you firmly
warn your colleague about this issue: ----

secenekler.A:
If you really believe in your merits, don’t waste
time worrying about the handicaps you may
need to overcome.
secenekler.B:
Rushing into such a major change without
focusing on details could seriously harm
your future security. You must proceed more
cautiously.
secenekler.C:
You have great ideas, and sometimes it’s wise
to act quickly before opportunities disappear. But
you seem to ignore the dangers, don’t you?
secenekler.D:
Building your own company sounds exciting!
You should first design a catchy logo and a
strong brand image if you want to succeed.
secenekler.E:
No one can predict what will happen, so it’d be
better for you to follow your instincts rather than
contemplate risk factors.

soru:
Your teammate in a group project submits his
part very late, which delays everyone else’s
work. This has happened more than once. You
want to express your frustration but still keep
everyone cooperating. So you say without being
offensive: ----

secenekler.A:
You clearly don’t care about completing this
project on time as much as the rest of us do.
secenekler.B:
I know things can get busy, but it really sets us
back when we don’t stick to the timeline.
secenekler.C:
If something’s making it hard to meet the
deadlines, find your own way to handle it instead
of asking for help.
secenekler.D:
This is the third time you’ve held us all up.
Maybe you’re not cut out for group work.
secenekler.E:
Why even bother assigning you tasks if they are
going to be late every time?

soru:
One of your friends has decided to apply for a
challenging scholarship abroad, but he is quite
nervous and unsure whether he can earn it. To
support and encourage your friend, you say: ----

secenekler.A:
Scholarships are extremely competitive. Maybe
you should reconsider and apply next year when
you’re more prepared.
secenekler.B:
If you don’t feel fully ready, there’s no shame in
giving up now. It’s better than facing rejection
later.
secenekler.C:
Many people apply for scholarships without
much thought. So, you should aim for the ones
that you can easily earn.
secenekler.D:
I know it’s a lot of pressure, but based on your
good qualities, I’ve no doubt that you’ll be
eligible for that scholarship. Just give it a try!
secenekler.E:
Applying isn’t easy, and you’ll probably have to
deal with too much stress. Make sure you know
what you’re getting into.

soru:
You are the organiser of a reading club that
takes place twice a month. One of the members
keeps attending the meetings without reading
the books and interrupts everyone with her
questions. You warned her before, but it seems
she has ignored your warning. So, you politely
suggest: ----

secenekler.A:
Why did you join our club if you knew that you
could not spare some time to read the assigned
books?
secenekler.B:
It might be a good idea for you to take a break
from the club until you have time to read the
books and participate actively.
secenekler.C:
I’ve tried to warn you but you didn’t listen.
I’m afraid I can’t allow you to attend our club
anymore.
secenekler.D:
I know you’re trying to keep up with the club
despite your problems with time management.
I wish you chose a less challenging hobby for
yourself.
secenekler.E:
The other members told me to drop you from the
club. But I’ll try to convince them to give you one
last chance if you promise to read the books.

soru:
You have been attending an art class for several
months, and once again, it conflicts with your
work schedule. You politely ask your boss if
you can once again leave work early to attend
the class. However, she is displeased with
your request to leave work early again, so she
sarcastically says: ----

secenekler.A:
You’ve missed too much work already. I won’t
allow you to leave early because it negatively
impacts all of your co-workers, not to mention
the customers.
secenekler.B:
Your art classes seem to be taking a lot of your
time. Isn’t there a way for you to rearrange your
classes so that you don’t escape your work
responsibilities?
secenekler.C:
Well, with all those art classes for which you
neglected your work, you must have been a
brilliant artist by now. Don’t you think so?
secenekler.D:
I can’t believe you’d even think of coming to
me with a request like that though I’ve warned
you many times before not to skip work for your
personal pursuits.
secenekler.E:
That’s tragic because one of your colleagues just
asked me if she could leave work early today.
You both seem to forget the requirements of
working here.

soru:
Your friend and you are on a sightseeing tour
and decide to take a taxi to head to your next
destination. Unfortunately, traffic is terrible
and you are hardly moving on the congested
roads. Your friend, annoyed by the situation,
sarcastically says: ----

secenekler.A:
Well, isn’t this something? If we’d known how
long this was going to take, I guess we would’ve
been standing still.
secenekler.B:
I’m so disappointed to see such a popular
destination having the worst road infrastructure.
secenekler.C:
Today, we’re going to set a record for the fewest
number of places visited in the longest amount
of time.
secenekler.D:
You know, today’s been tiring, so, at least, we
can take this time to be off our feet and rest for
just a little while.
secenekler.E:
I think this place has the worst traffic I’ve ever
seen! It’s interesting that none of the guidebooks
make any mention of it.

soru:
Your friend at university wants to drop out of
school to become an e-sports player. While he
shows promise, you know his long-term dream
has been to become a mechanical engineer. You
gently discourage him by saying: ----

secenekler.A:
You know, there are already enough talented
e-sports players and not enough engineers.
Plus, just think of how much money you can
make.
secenekler.B:
An e-sports player? Last week you were telling
me that you wanted to go to trade school. You
can’t be serious.
secenekler.C:
Your parents will be disappointed if you do that,
you know. It’s so important for them that you
become a successful engineer.
secenekler.D:
I know you’re excited about it, but maybe it’s
best if you focus on your ultimate goal. You can
always spare time for e-sports as a hobby.
secenekler.E:
Instead of trying to make a career out of every
new idea you have, why don’t you make a list of
pros and cons for each?

soru:
Your co-worker has been chosen for a
promotion, and you think she is well-qualified
for it. But she’s nervous about having extra
responsibilities and aware that she has a lot to
learn. To reassure her, you say: ----

secenekler.A:
Well, to be honest I think I might have been a
slightly better choice for the job, but I’m glad you
got the promotion.
secenekler.B:
You will have more responsibilities, and it might
be challenging. You probably won’t have much
time for yourself after this. I would be hesitant if I
were you.
secenekler.C:
You said before that they didn’t take you
seriously around here, and now look what has
happened. I hope you’re ready.
secenekler.D:
You’ve got this. They chose you for this new
position because you’re the best possible
candidate for the job.
secenekler.E:
Instead of celebrating, let’s think about all the
possible challenges you might face, so that there
won’t be any surprises later on.

soru:
Your company is planning to hire a new
employee. One recruitment committee member
insists on hiring someone with only technical
skills, but you think that would not suffice. So,
you highly encourage them to consider other
qualities too by saying: ----

secenekler.A:
Why don’t companies practice what they want
other people to do? Shouldering some of the
responsibilities could make what we claim more
reasonable.
secenekler.B:
Technical skills are necessary, but we need to
consider things like emotional intelligence as
well. People with emotional intelligence tend
to be more productive, which matters to us.
Wouldn’t you agree?
secenekler.C:
Why shouldn’t we take a chance on someone
with fewer technical skills? We can train them on
their way to the top.
secenekler.D:
The company expects people to be motivated,
and giving employees responsibility for their
work pays off big time in generating an engaged
workforce.
secenekler.E:
People at a certain age can manage themselves
and require less training and supervision to get
the job done. Why would we waste our time
educating people?

soru:
You are working on a group project. One of the
group members is not contributing much, as
she is busy organising a birthday party. You
want to encourage your group member to be
responsible for her share of the work, so you
tactfully say: ----

secenekler.A:
I know how important that birthday party is to
you, but I also strongly urge you to strike a
balance between your project and other tasks.
secenekler.B:
We know it is difficult to throw a big birthday
party, so why don’t we all stop working on the
project and help you with the arrangements?
secenekler.C:
I wish you had told us earlier how important this
party is. We could have persuaded our teacher
not to assign this project now.
secenekler.D:
I think you’ll have to start working on the
project, or else I will have to report your lack of
commitment to the group to the teacher.
secenekler.E:
Why don’t you talk to the teacher and see
whether you could leave this group and work
on a different project when you have more free
time?

soru:
- 45. sorularda, boş bırakılan yere, parçada
anlam bütünlüğünü sağlamak için getirilebilecek
cümleyi bulunuz.
1.
Women are roughly twice as likely as men to
suffer from stress-related psychiatric disorders,
according to epidemiological analyses. The big
question has always been: Why? Some experts
argue that cultural factors are at least partly
responsible. For instance, women may be more
willing than men to seek help for mental illness,
making their cases more likely to be counted.
---- Scientists are uncovering telling differences
in the ways that male and female brains react
and adapt to stress.

secenekler.A:
But new evidence from research suggests that
biology may also play an important role.
secenekler.B:
However, scientists have studied more males
than females – even when investigating
disorders.
secenekler.C:
Also, it is not only the stress-related disorders
that are more prevalent among women than
men.
secenekler.D:
Similarly, animal studies have revealed
significant differences in stress responses.
secenekler.E:
In fact, research has linked uncontrolled stress
to a wide range of mental health problems.

soru:
There are more than 600 ethnic or tribal groups
in Africa, and only 53 countries. Many of today’s
national boundaries were created in the late 19th
century by colonial rulers. ---- As a result, tribes
are often split between different countries. The
Ewe people, for example, are divided between
Ghana and Togo. After independence, it has
often proved difficult to create unity among the
different peoples in one country.

secenekler.A:
Africa is home to about 849 million people –
more than one in eight of the world’s population.
secenekler.B:
Also, groups of nomadic people, who tend to
roam together across many countries, are found
throughout western Africa.
secenekler.C:
The most heavily urbanized region in Africa
is northern Africa, and Cairo, in Egypt, is the
largest city on the continent.
secenekler.D:
Borders sometimes follow natural features, such
as rivers, but often they just follow straight lines
on a map.
secenekler.E:
The war between the Hutu and Tutsi peoples
has forced thousands of people to leave their
homes.

soru:
The coffee tree is an evergreen. It grows in
about 70 countries that offer suitable climates
and altitudes. ---- They are picked from the tree
during harvest – they contain two seeds, which
after processing become coffee beans. The main
commercially grown coffee tree species are
Arabica and Robusta. While Robustas are
high-yielding and resistant to pests and
diseases, producing coffee cherries with rustic
flavour, Arabicas are generally superior in
flavour.

secenekler.A:
As botanists discover new species with
interesting flavours, the family tree of coffee
continues to grow.
secenekler.B:
The trees are cultivated with care, and grow for
about 3-5 years before they flower and produce
fruit, known as coffee cherries.
secenekler.C:
The movement of hot and cold air influences
how the coffee cherries mature and taste.
secenekler.D:
Many coffee varieties are genetically similar, but
have acquired different regional or local names.
secenekler.E:
The look and flavour of coffee are influenced
by many forces, such as soil, sun exposure and
rainfall patterns.

soru:
---- A baby was born with a small head caused
by incomplete brain development. The mother
likely caught the virus in Brazil. Meanwhile, the
US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
have advised pregnant women against travel to
countries affected by the Zika virus.

secenekler.A:
It is foreseen that the US will have to face deaths
caused by the Zika virus in the near future.
secenekler.B:
The first case of brain damage linked to the Zika
virus on the US soil has been reported in Hawaii.
secenekler.C:
The effects of the Zika virus have diminished
dramatically in the recent years.
secenekler.D:
Brain damages caused by the Zika virus cannot
be treated for the time being.
secenekler.E:
Scientists have estimated that the Zika virus may
spread across Europe besides the US.

soru:
Plants and livestock need air, water, and
nourishment to stay alive. If a plant does not have
the kind of soil it needs, it may die. Similarly,
animals also need to have the right climate and
the right food to survive. Farmers try to raise the
kinds of livestock and plants that will do well in
their particular region. ---- For example, many
farmers in dry areas use irrigation, or artificial
watering.

secenekler.A:
Farmers raise crops and livestock in every
climate and in all kinds of different soil.
secenekler.B:
Plants and animals also supply such natural
materials as cotton, flax, wool, and hides.
secenekler.C:
Agriculture provides the food and many of the
raw materials that humans need to survive.
secenekler.D:
Some regions receive a lot of sunlight or rainfall
while others have colder or drier weather.
secenekler.E:
If they do not have perfect natural conditions,
they try to create the best conditions possible.

soru:
A scientist at Japan’s Osaka University built a
robot for one purpose: to pretend to listen to
you. When two or more are placed together,
they will simulate people having a conversation.
If a human attempts to join in, the robots will
smile, nod, and respond to comments by saying
things like “I see” or “interesting point”. They
will not actually understand what has been
said, but will appear to. ---- But the motivation
behind the robot was to try and model the subtle
body language and polite niceties that are so
important to conversation.

secenekler.A:
This is, of course, an entirely pointless
achievement.
secenekler.B:
Robots that seem more ‘human’ and less
intimidating are being built.
secenekler.C:
Equally important for roboticists is an
understanding of human psychology.
secenekler.D:
The team hope to make robots with more
realistic behaviours.
secenekler.E:
There must be a balance between the
psychological and the scientific when building a
robot.

soru:
Forests, conserved land, and natural habitats
are not important just for the sake of saving
trees and animals. Forests and all greenery
are important in keeping the climate in check.
Plants take in the carbon in the atmosphere
and give back oxygen, and older trees hold
on to that carbon, storing it for the duration of
their lives. By taking in carbon dioxide, they are
reducing the greenhouse effect. ---- And now,
deforestation is responsible for about a quarter
of greenhouse gas emissions.

secenekler.A:
In other words, greenhouse gases trap heat in
the Earth’s atmosphere, which increases global
average temperature.
secenekler.B:
Unfortunately, many of the world’s forests
have been cut down to make way for farmland,
highways, and cities.
secenekler.C:
Yet, some countries have chosen sustainable
development plans instead of economic plans
that would produce greenhouse gases.
secenekler.D:
In fact, it is not only the trees and oceans that
store carbon, soil does, too, and by exposing
the carbon to the oxygen in the air, it helps to
produce carbon dioxide.
secenekler.E:
Although the soil on a treeless hillside washes
away in a mudslide, a tree-covered hillside’s soil
stays put.

soru:
Children’s furniture stresses the social position
of the child in relation to both the environment
and to adults. ---- The very existence of
children’s furniture promotes the child’s
position because it is the property of the child
and it also physically occupies space – a choice
that excludes other furniture and reflects a
priority, stressing the child’s social importance.
If a child has a piece of furniture of his or her
own, this acknowledges the status and rank
of the child. The special form of children’s
furniture signals that childhood is considered an
important period.

secenekler.A:
Furniture made especially for children is
not a modern phenomenon but has existed
independent of the ways in which adult views of
children have changed.
secenekler.B:
Having an individual piece of furniture for
children indicates the child’s status and the right
to status in society.
secenekler.C:
Children’s furniture has historically been defined
not just by scale but also by aesthetic purposes.
secenekler.D:
The design of children’s furniture is influenced
by period, material, form, function, pedagogical
views, and children’s games and status.
secenekler.E:
Of the children’s furniture that has survived from
earlier periods, chairs tend to show the most
variety.

soru:
Following the last Ice Age, humans had to adapt
their diet and ways of life. While mobility was
usual, in favourable areas with exceptional
resources, communities could become settled.
Hunter-gatherers used a wide variety of foods.
---- For example, herd animals moved between
summer upland and winter lowland pastures,
marine fish and birds migrated seasonally, and
woodlands produced autumn fruits and spring
bulbs. However, other food sources, such as
shellfish, small mammals, and freshwater fish,
could be found all year round.

secenekler.A:
Bones and shells recovered from archaeological
sites are the most obvious remains of what
hunter-gatherers ate.
secenekler.B:
In some favoured regions, early humans could
remain in one location with abundant resources.
secenekler.C:
Hunter-gatherers in warmer areas often hunted
gazelle, the most common mammal in the
region.
secenekler.D:
In most regions, some foods were available in
different places at certain times of year.
secenekler.E:
Hunter-gatherers selected environments offering
a diversity of food sources, such as lakes, rivers
and coasts.

soru:
Caffeine is a bitter substance found in the
beans, leaves, and fruits of plants, where it
acts as a natural pesticide. It is found in a wide
variety of products, including coffee, tea, soft
drinks, candy, and desserts. Caffeine acts
as a mood enhancer and provides energy.
---- When heavy coffee drinkers reduce their
caffeine intake, for example, they often report
being irritable, restless, and drowsy, as well
as experiencing strong headaches, and these
symptoms may last up to a week.

secenekler.A:
While most experts feel that consuming small
amounts of caffeine during pregnancy is safe,
larger amounts of caffeine can be harmful to the
foetus.
secenekler.B:
It causes accelerated heart and breathing rates,
and increases in blood sugar accompanied by
decreases in appetite, thus it is used to stay
awake and control weight.
secenekler.C:
There are many mixed messages about caffeine
in the media, and it can be difficult to find
information that relates to you.
secenekler.D:
Although food authorities list caffeine as a
safe food substance, it has at least some
characteristics of an addictive substance.
secenekler.E:
For those who love and appreciate the flavour
of good coffee, but would like to reduce their
caffeine intake, there are options.

soru:
Sociology is one of a number of social sciences
which attempt to understand and explain the
behaviour of human beings. Unlike some social
sciences, it does not confine itself to one
particular area of society. ---- It is hard to think
of any significant area of life which has never
been the subject of a sociological study.

secenekler.A:
Indeed, sociologists are concerned with a vast
range of topics including shopping, popular
music, poverty, and migration.
secenekler.B:
In sociology, then, it is essential to understand
the social context in which human behaviour
takes place.
secenekler.C:
A change in society such as the introduction
of new technology can lead to new ways of
behaving.
secenekler.D:
Socialisation is a lifelong process which
continues as people change their jobs or roles
and as society itself changes.
secenekler.E:
At the most basic level, sociology involves
understanding the culture of the society in
which social action occurs.

soru:
Microwave ovens do not directly cook food;
what they do is heat water. The frequency of
microwaves happens to be just right for exciting
water molecules. ---- Nearly all food contains
water, but microwaves will not cook completely
dry food like cornflakes, rice or pasta.

secenekler.A:
Microwaves are a form of electromagnetic
radiation that sits on the spectrum between radio
waves and infrared light.
secenekler.B:
By spreading their energy evenly through food,
the microwaves heat the water in it and the hot
water cooks the food.
secenekler.C:
Microwave cookery is similar to heating food
in a normal oven, except that the microwaves
penetrate deeper and more quickly.
secenekler.D:
The molecules in the centre of your soup are not
heated any quicker than those on the outside.
secenekler.E:
Exciting the water molecules means that the
food rarely gets much hotter than 100°C, at
which water boils.

soru:
Until now, there has not been a comprehensive
map of soil bacteria, but a team of scientists
recently took the first steps toward creating one
and found out something surprising along the
way. These researchers collected nearly 300
soil samples from 18 countries and as many
different environments as possible. ---- However,
the scientists found that across these different
environments on Earth, a relatively small
number of bacteria species dominated.

secenekler.A:
These tiny organisms, which populate every
environment, play active roles in many of Earth’s
biological processes.
secenekler.B:
They create acidic environments, decompose
dead organisms and release gases.
secenekler.C:
They were expecting to find a diverse array of
bacteria species spanning different terrains.
secenekler.D:
With this new bacteria list, scientists have a
starting point for studying the complex web of
ecosystem.
secenekler.E:
Of the thousands of individual species of
bacteria, only 20 percent of those are known to
scientists.

soru:
The carbon cycle is the natural system
that, ideally, creates a balance between
carbon emitters (such as humans) and
carbon absorbers (such as trees) so that the
atmosphere does not contain an increasing
amount of carbon dioxide. It is a huge process
that involves oceans, land, and air. ---- You can
think of it almost as the Earth breathing in and
out.

secenekler.A:
The exchange of carbon dioxide between the
ocean and the air happens at the surface of the
water.
secenekler.B:
The seas’ ability to absorb carbon dioxide has
long been known to scientists.
secenekler.C:
The carbon cycle is called “in balance” when
roughly the same amount of carbon that is being
pumped into the air is being sucked out by
something else.
secenekler.D:
Given the important role that carbon dioxide
plays in warming the Earth, you may be
surprised by how little of it is in the atmosphere.
secenekler.E:
Carbon dioxide is composed of one carbon atom
and two oxygen atoms, connected by double
bonds.

soru:
The creation of revolutionary products or
practices has no timetable. Great minds
give birth to innovations as inspiration hits,
necessity requires, or happenstance would
have it. ---- The Renaissance, for instance, was
a period of great intellectual exploration, an
era of innovation in arts, philosophy, medicine,
engineering, and science. Inventions of the
Renaissance include the printing press and
movable type. It was also at this time that
Leonardo da Vinci (1452–1519) drew the first
plans for a flying machine, a precursor to planes
and jets that would be devised and developed
centuries later.

secenekler.A:
Human progress is now taking place at an
unprecedented pace.
secenekler.B:
Nevertheless, the history of the human race can
conceivably be called the story of innovation.
secenekler.C:
However, there have been a number of
specifically fruitful periods of invention
throughout history.
secenekler.D:
Also, their other inventions go beyond basic
human needs to enhance human interaction.
secenekler.E:
Furthermore, the invention of the electric bulb is
said to be a pure coincidence.

soru:
The Aral Sea is a saltwater body in central Asia.
It is bordered by Kazakhstan in the north and
Uzbekistan in the south. The Aral Sea once
covered an area of 68,000 square kilometres.
However, it started to shrink during the second
half of the 1900s, as most of the inflowing river
water was used for irrigation before it reached
the sea. The sea also loses water through
evaporation. ---- The Aral has therefore shrunk
drastically in its area and volume. By the end of
the 1900s, the Aral Sea had lost so much water
that the exposed land divided the sea into three
separate parts.

secenekler.A:
The Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers, which are
mainly used for irrigation, are the sea’s two main
sources of inflowing water.
secenekler.B:
The fishing industry along the Aral Sea has also
been virtually destroyed due to a number of
factors.
secenekler.C:
Also called Lake Aral, the Aral Sea is situated
more than 400 kilometres east of the Caspian
Sea.
secenekler.D:
Scientists view the changes to the Aral Sea as
a serious threat to the local environment and
human health.
secenekler.E:
Because there is not much rainfall, this water is
not replaced fast enough to maintain the water
level.

soru:
Several studies have shown that dancing can
help to increase feelings of self-worth. In one
2007 study, researchers found that children
aged between 11 and 14 who took part in
creative movement classes reported improved
self-esteem, motivation, and more positive
attitudes towards dance, as well as better
physical fitness. Dancing has also been shown
to reduce feelings of depression. ---- In a study,
dancing characterised by relaxed, free-flowing
movements helped to improve mood, whereas
dancing in a physically contracted way had the
opposite effect.

secenekler.A:
However, different dancing styles have had
different effects on people.
secenekler.B:
In fact, people are communicating with potential
mates when they dance.
secenekler.C:
Just five minutes of freestyle dancing can
increase creativity.
secenekler.D:
Therefore, dancers show improvements both in
mood and problem-solving.
secenekler.E:
In addition, group dancing can increase a
person’s threshold for pain.

soru:
Technology is a powerful component of the
modern world. Without technology, many of the
most significant feats of the 20th century could
not have been achieved, such as sending people
to the Moon, erecting skyscrapers, damming
enormous rivers, and communicating with
friends around the world. ---- We use technology
to house, clothe, feed, entertain, and transport
ourselves. It is a crucial component of our work,
play, education, shopping, and travel.

secenekler.A:
Our decisions about how to develop technology,
and when and where to use it, can make a great
difference for future economic, political, and
social well-being.
secenekler.B:
Not only does technology shape our tools,
devices, buildings, and cars, but it also affects
our values, ideas, and beliefs.
secenekler.C:
However, it is essential for all of us to realise that
technology can have destructive consequences
when misused.
secenekler.D:
Though less often recognised, the most
significant power of technology is its assistance
in so many aspects of our everyday lives.
secenekler.E:
In order to direct technology in the most
beneficial ways, we need to know more than
science and engineering traditionally offer.

soru:
The line that separates one country from
another is called a border. Sometimes these
follow a natural feature, such as a mountain
range or a river. On other occasions they follow
a straight line, ignoring physical features. ----
However, if there is a conflict, borders may be
heavily guarded, and it is often difficult to move
from one country to another.

secenekler.A:
The longest undefended border in the world runs
between the US and Canada.
secenekler.B:
Politics can play an important role in the creation
of borders, for example when one country seeks
independence from another.
secenekler.C:
When countries are on friendly terms, borders
can be little more than lines on a map, easily
crossed.
secenekler.D:
Generally you can only cross the borders
between countries if you have either a passport
or the appropriate paperwork.
secenekler.E:
While some countries, like Greenland, do not
have borders, other countries, like Switzerland,
are surrounded by them.

soru:
The relationship between humans and dogs
has been in existence for over 10,000 years,
and shows no signs of weakening. But it is
changing, as the traditional tasks that dogs
perform have been supplemented by new roles.
autism-spectrum disorders benefit from the
company of a dog. Some such children form
intense relationships with animals, seemingly
finding them easier to relate to. ---- Otherwise,
children tend to ignore pets that were there
when they were babies.

secenekler.A:
However, in order to be the most effective, the
dog has to be obtained when the child is old
enough to interact with it.
secenekler.B:
Getting a dog may not automatically make
children healthier, but you need to train it well for
that.
secenekler.C:
In fact, dogs need to be able to read a child’s
body language in order to get the best out of
their interactive natures.
secenekler.D:
That’s why the capacity of pets to bring people
together is made use of in many kinds of
therapy.
secenekler.E:
It is not known precisely how this occurs, but
a dog’s ability to detect minute changes in the
child’s body must play a part.

soru:
To form a thunderstorm from a convective
cloud, several conditions are necessary. ---- In
an unstable atmosphere, the air temperature
drops rapidly with height, meaning any bubble
of air that begins rising and cooling will remain
warmer than its surroundings. At every point
in its ascent the rising air acts like a hot air
balloon. Since it is warmer and less dense than
the surrounding air, it continues to rise.

secenekler.A:
Severe thunderstorms also may form tornadoes,
columns of air spinning at extremely high wind
speeds.
secenekler.B:
However, among them, most importantly the
atmosphere must be unpredictable.
secenekler.C:
Severe thunderstorms may include hail,
tornadoes, and damaging straight line winds.
secenekler.D:
The most severe cause of flooding usually
follows short but very intensive thunderstorms.
secenekler.E:
In addition, lightning is a giant spark caused by a
build-up of static electrical charges.

soru:
If you use a mobile phone, drive a car or watch
a television, the chances are that at least one
of those objects will have been made in Korea.
Korea is one of Asia’s ‘tiger’ economies, a
provider of high technology for the world. ----
However, it is not how Koreans see themselves,
for Korea has always been pivotal in relations
between China and Japan, and it has a long
tradition of technological innovation. It was
Korea, for example, that pioneered movable
metal type, and it did so well before it was
utilised in Europe.

secenekler.A:
It has long been divided between a communist
north and a capitalist south, severely hindering
technological developments.
secenekler.B:
By the year 900, Korea was already a rich,
urbanised country and a major player in global
trade, based at the end of the famous Silk Road.
secenekler.C:
Economic relations since the early 1990s have
significantly benefited Chinese start-ups in the
absorption of advanced technology.
secenekler.D:
Most countries see the technology gap between
the Western world and Korea as increasing.
secenekler.E:
The outside world commonly view Korea as a
relatively new player in the global economy.

soru:
History can be written from many different
viewpoints. A 19th-century European writing
shortly after the French Revolution is likely to
have very different interests from a Chinese
bureaucrat living in the 2nd century BCE, or a
10th-century Muslim traveller. Moreover, the
interpretation of facts is always open to dispute,
and historians often disagree about how one
fact is linked with another. ---- The perspective of
chroniclers such as the French scholar Geoffrey
Villehardouin on the Fourth Crusade, is very
different from that of his contemporary on the
opposing side, the Arab historian Ibn al-Athir.

secenekler.A:
Throughout history itself, we see evidence of
different ideas about the same events.
secenekler.B:
History is an incomplete puzzle, made up of
fragments from the evidence that is available.
secenekler.C:
Names for eras and ages may not necessarily
have been used at the time, but now they serve
to break down the past into convenient blocks.
secenekler.D:
We can never directly experience the past — we
can never know how it felt to be a gladiator fighting
in the Colosseum of ancient Rome.
secenekler.E:
Historians ask not only ‘what happened?’, but
also ‘why did it happen?’ and ‘what were the
consequences?’.

soru:
How do humans and the environment affect
each other? There are three key concepts
to the interaction between humans and the
environment: humans adapt to the environment;
humans modify the environment; and humans
depend on the environment. ---- For example,
clearing a forest for farming produces food,
but also destroys trees. Burning coal provides
energy, but also pollutes the air.

secenekler.A:
Most of the changes people make on the
environment are intentional, such as building
wide tunnels through mountains.
secenekler.B:
Humans have always had a huge impact on the
environment, by changing or trying to blend in
with their surroundings.
secenekler.C:
The environment provides food and shelter
to humans and various sources of energy to
maintain their lives.
secenekler.D:
Some particular actions that humans carry out
have pluses and minuses for them and the
environment.
secenekler.E:
The environment can shape laws, customs,
lifestyles, and economic activities of humans to a
great extent.

soru:
Mixing the metals copper and tin creates bronze.
Bronze, like other mixtures of metals, is called
an alloy. Bronze is harder and stronger than
copper. ---- For these reasons bronze is often
used to make tools and machinery. Bronze is
also used to make electrical hardware, springs,
fasteners, and coins. Bronze has been the most
popular metal for making statues and other
artistic objects since ancient times.

secenekler.A:
Bronze also changes colours when exposed to
air and water.
secenekler.B:
Bronze is also used for making life-sized
sculptures of people and animals.
secenekler.C:
It also does not wear away as easily as either
copper or tin.
secenekler.D:
The earliest bronzes date back to the late 4th
millennium BCE.
secenekler.E:
Bronze is the traditional name for a broad range
of alloys of copper.

soru:
Merchandising is the process by which goods
are produced in association with a media
product, which can then be sold to consumers.
Many successful films, such as Star Wars
or Spiderman, have greatly increased their
revenues by licensing the ideas, script, images
or music from the film to companies which
will release products associated with the
film. Associated with Star Wars, for instance,
are toys, books, clothes and games. While
merchandising is not new and has been
connected to a range of artists in the past, the
process is now seen as central to promotion of
media products themselves. ---- For example,
computer games have toys and books
associated with them and rock groups sell
T-shirts.

secenekler.A:
There was an explosion of goods associated
with the rock group The Beatles in the 1960s.
secenekler.B:
Merchandising is clearest in film, though other
forms of media seek to maximise revenues from
their successes in the same way.
secenekler.C:
In a few cases, revenue from merchandising has
matched or even exceeded revenue from the
original media.
secenekler.D:
When you promote a product too much,
consumers may become uninterested in buying
the goods.
secenekler.E:
Filmmaking is a collaborative process, but the
nature of the normal structure of how media is
produced is questioned.

soru:
Adolescence is an exciting time. It is also a
time that can be very confusing. Boys and girls
become much more interested in each other. ----
In fact, during adolescence, most boys and girls
care a lot about what other adolescents think
of them. They may also be very concerned with
how they fit into their world. Often adolescents
choose to spend time with their friends rather
than with their families.

secenekler.A:
When it is time, boys grow facial hair, develop
stronger muscles, and their voices deepen.
secenekler.B:
At the same time, they may worry about their
appearance, and they are sometimes easily
embarrassed.
secenekler.C:
As adolescents grow emotionally, they begin
to take on new responsibilities and gain new
freedoms.
secenekler.D:
The fact that they act and think more
independently mean that they are on their way to
becoming adults.
secenekler.E:
Another change in the body during adolescence
is the development of the reproductive system.

soru:
Most teenagers and some adults experience
a skin condition called acne. It is caused by
changes inside the body which occur naturally
as a boy or girl reaches puberty, or matures. At
that time the body produces more of chemicals
called hormones. Some of those hormones
speed up the skin’s production of oil. ---- As the
oil gland under a blocked pore makes more oil,
the pore swells up to form a pimple.

secenekler.A:
However, there are treatments for clearing up
acne and ways of preventing acne from getting
worse.
secenekler.B:
There is very little a person can do to prevent
acne aside from washing the skin with a mild
soap.
secenekler.C:
The extra oil dumps together with dead skin cells
to clog pores, or tiny openings in the skin.
secenekler.D:
Some cases of acne are very mild and go away
without leaving any signs or scars.
secenekler.E:
Acne lesions are commonly known as pimples
and they occur especially on the face and neck.

soru:
Wall paintings in ancient Egyptian tombs show
that the people of Africa have made and played
musical instruments for thousands of years. ----
Arabs brought musical instruments and styles
that became part of the culture of North Africa,
the western savannah, and the eastern coast.
introduced Western instruments such as brass
horns. Urban musicians of modern Africa have
adopted Western electric instruments – guitar,
bass, and synthesiser – to create exciting
new music. Yet from the dance halls to the
rural farmlands, many musicians still play the
traditional instruments of Africa.

secenekler.A:
Over the centuries, the many invaders of Africa
introduced new instruments.
secenekler.B:
The knowledge of crafting musical instruments
has been passed on to younger generations by
the elderly.
secenekler.C:
A key feature of African music is when
instruments are played together.
secenekler.D:
African musicians have a long tradition
of inventing and making small handheld
instruments.
secenekler.E:
Most traditional musicians use their instruments
to create the distinctive sounds of African music.

soru:
A major goal of psychology is to predict
behaviour by understanding its causes. Making
predictions is difficult in part because people vary
and respond differently in different situations.
Individual differences are the variations among
people on physical or psychological dimensions.
---- Some people experience major negative
events, such as severe physical injuries or the
loss of significant others, without experiencing
much depression, whereas other people
experience severe depression for no apparent
reason.

secenekler.A:
For instance, although many people experience
some symptoms of depression in their lives, the
experience varies dramatically among people.
secenekler.B:
Other important individual differences include
intelligence, self-esteem, anxiety, aggression,
and conformity.
secenekler.C:
Because of the many individual variables that
influence behaviour, it is impossible to predict
who will become aggressive at school or at
work.
secenekler.D:
Likewise, people who go through similar painful
experiences tend to show common patterns of
behaviour.
secenekler.E:
Another reason why it is easy to predict
behaviour is that almost all human behaviour is
determined by a combination of many factors.

soru:
Children’s fascination with television has
concerned researchers and parents ever since
the medium was introduced. Much of the debate
has been focused on the effects of media
violence, which has resulted in much analysis
by psychologists and sociologists. ---- Other
worries have been about children’s physical
condition, such as too little exercise or the effect
of radiation from the screen on the brain or
eyes.

secenekler.A:
At the end of the 20th century, however, there
was a belief that television could be used for
enhancing children’s cognitive skills.
secenekler.B:
Therefore, unequal distribution of technological
resources in the world has created significant
differences in children’s social development over
the last decades.
secenekler.C:
Sometimes, television addiction has been
compared to other kinds of addiction children
are likely to develop, such as candies and toys.
secenekler.D:
Television has also been blamed for causing
negative effects on reading skills, and some
claim that spending too much time in front of the
television makes children antisocial.
secenekler.E:
There are a variety of programs promoting
prosocial behaviour, such as solving conflicts
without violence or strengthening children’s
self-confidence.

soru:
Our bodies contain a large amount of water,
typically between 50 and 70 percent of our
total body mass. The majority of this is in the
approximately 30 trillion cells that make up
the body, while the rest is in fluids such as the
blood. ---- This transport role is more obvious,
for example, when carrying material around
the bloodstream. It also lubricates, dissolves
valuable chemicals, and acts as a shock
absorber for organs, so it is hard to find a
part of the body where water does not play a
role — even bones are around one-third water.

secenekler.A:
